sections.title: DNS Fundamentals and How DNS Works
keyTopics: DNS terminologies (registrar, zone file, NS, TLD, SLD)
Root, TLD and SLD DNS servers
DNS resolution flow and TTL caching
sections.objective: Explain how a DNS query resolves a hostname through local, root, TLD and SLD servers, and identify what makes Route 53 an authoritative, fully managed DNS service.

sections.title: Records, Hosted Zones, TTL and Alias Records
keyTopics: Alias record targets and ACEM exclusion
sections.objective: Choose between CNAME and Alias records for AWS resources and the zone apex, and distinguish public from private hosted zones and high versus low TTL trade-offs.

sections.title: Routing Policies Part 1: Simple, Weighted, Latency
sections.objective: Select the correct routing policy (simple, weighted, or latency-based) for a scenario and explain how weight values and latency measurements affect the answer returned.

sections.title: Health Checks and Failover Routing
keyTopics: Health checks for private hosted zones
sections.objective: Design automated DNS failover using health checks, including calculated health checks and CloudWatch alarm-based checks for private resources, and apply failover routing as active-passive.

sections.title: Routing Policies Part 2: Geolocation, Geoproximity, IP-based, Multi-Value
sections.objective: Distinguish geolocation from latency-based routing, apply geoproximity bias and IP-based CIDR routing, and decide when multi-value answers are appropriate instead of a load balancer.

sections.title: Domain Registrar vs DNS Service and Hybrid DNS
keyTopics: Hybrid DNS between VPC and on-premises
sections.objective: Explain how to use Route 53 as DNS service with a third-party registrar and choose inbound versus outbound Resolver endpoints for hybrid DNS between VPC and on-premises networks.

notes: Section boundaries follow slide concepts: DNS basics (194-198), records/zones/alias (199-206), first routing policies (207-210), health checks + failover (211-215), remaining routing policies (216-221), registrar/hybrid DNS (222-227). Exam guide emphasis: Task 2.2 tests failover routing, health check types, and alarm-based checks for private resources; Task 3.4 tests latency-based and geolocation selection plus geoproximity bias. Background additions for exam correctness: Route 53 record Alias targets and Multi-Value returning up to 8 healthy records appear in source; always distinguish "DNS responds to queries" from actual traffic routing as the source warns, since distractors reuse load balancing language.
